pull.title: mining: use steady clock for waitNext timeout
pull.body:
Follow up suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36791#discussion_r4568050151.

`waitNext` measures its timeout and 1-second fee tick with the wall clock, while `waitTipChanged` uses the steady clock. This means a wall clock jump changes how long `waitNext` waits, and it never times out while mocktime is frozen.

Use the steady clock for the deadline and tick. `NodeClock` is kept only for the testnet 20-minute rule, which must compare node time with the tip's timestamp.

Ideally, start with the one that should be merged first.

tACK a02c31ca22e7c76fdd737d36b16140bbb618c140

Nit. #36862 has been merged, so a rebase and/or a description tweak would ease review.

tACK a02c31c

I first thought `MockableSteadyClock` would be better here, to match #36922 (which uses it for the gbt cache age) and so tests could still control the timeout. But deadline and `now + tick` go into `wait_until`, which waits in real time, so a mocked clock could drift from the actual wait? So `steady_clock` seems good here as it matches `WaitTipChanged`.

nit: the rationale from the PR description would be useful in the commit body.

I think this will conflict trivially with my #36940 on the deadline line.

Code review a02c31ca22e7c76fdd737d36b16140bbb618c140

The rounding issue in my inline comment also reminds me that we should probably document that timestamp rolling needs extra care on testnet3 and testnet4.

E.g. a miner could get a template a few seconds before the rule kicks in and find a solution before waitNext() returns, which `submitSolution()` would reject. 

```cpp
/**
 * Block header. Its nTime is a suggested timestamp; submitSolution()
 * takes the final one.
 *
 * @note On testnet3 and testnet4 a block more than 20 minutes after the
 *       previous block MUST use the minimum difficulty. Never roll more
 *       than 20 minutes past the previous block's time on these networks,
 *       or the block is invalid (bad-diffbits).
 *       waitNext() returns a minimum difficulty template once that point
 *       is reached.     
 */
virtual CBlockHeader getBlockHeader() = 0;
```

IIUC testnet5 gets rid of this rule:

Thanks for the reviews! Force-pushed cac1ef8cdb166255997b0e119b825b85df8baa06 addressing @Sjors  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36870#pullrequestreview-6023988836 fixing the testnet3 and testnet4 adjustment rule, use `SteadyClock` and document timestamp rolling. Also addressed @enochaz https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36870#pullrequestreview-6007764096 to add PR description to the commit body.

Also added Co-Authors

ACK cac1ef8cdb166255997b0e119b825b85df8baa06

Ironically Ralph's review is hard to read by agents because the site blocks bots.

> The testnet 20-minute note overstates the consensus rule

This is true, but the instruction to never roll testnet3 and testnet4 blocks more than 20 minutes is fine despite that.

> Frozen-clock coverage never exercises a positive waitNext() timeout

This sounds like adding test coverage for tests, I would ignore it.
While reviewing this, my agent noticed https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36983. It's easier to fix it on top of this PR, but that can be a followup.
